title: an arrow-arm `case` clause is rejected even when the rest of the switch uses the required colon-delimited form — one switch must not carry two clause grammars
notes: Obligation: specification/control-flow.mdx, 'Switch': 'Switch syntax MUST use the same `switch`, `case`, `default`, and colon-delimited clauses as TypeScript. Smithers MUST NOT introduce a separate arrow-arm switch grammar.' This case exists separately from arrow-arm-switch-grammar-is-rejected because the two shapes answer different questions. That case asks whether the arrow form is accepted at all; this one asks whether it is a real grammar — a construct that composes with the documented one — which is what turns 'lenient error recovery' into 'a second switch grammar Smithers does not have'. The `js` xfail here is RETIRED: the reference used to lower both clause grammars into one switch, giving the arrow arm the same value semantics as the colon arm, and now rejects the arrow at its own position with the clause rule in poc/src/language/semantic.ts. Exactly one diagnostic is expected: the colon `default:` beside it is the required form and must not be swept up with it.
